The Brooks Family

Our passion is to provide excellent quality, ranch-raised, grass fed beef while maintaining the cowboy tradition of animal and land stewardship. Brandon Brooks comes from a Montana ranching family that has been raising beef under the Big Sky for 100 years. His great-grandfather came to Montana on a cattle drive from Texas and never left, establishing a family tradition of cowboy heritage that Brandon and Jessa continue to this day.

Located in Northwest Montana on the banks of the Flathead River, the Brooks Ranch raises grass fed and finished, hormone free Angus beef. We raise our cattle south of Flathead Lake in the Mission Valley for the first few months of the year until they move to summer pasture in the Madison Valley next to Yellowstone National Park. Their time away from the Mission Valley allows for high-protein, pesticide-free alfalfa hay to be farmed and stored for their winter forage.

The ranch in Ronan, MT.

Grass fed

OUR PROMISE IS OUR COWS ARE NEVER FED ANYTHING OTHER THAN RANGE LAND GRASSES AND PESTICIDE-FREE ALFALFA THEIR WHOLE LIVES. OUR COWS HAVE AN EXCELLENT AND DIVERSE DIET THAT LENDS TO THE COMPLEX BLACK ANGUS FLAVOR. 

Headed to new pasture in Ennis, MT.

Free Range

GENERAL RULE OF THUMB IS A COW AND CALF PAIR NEEDS 1.5-2 ACRES OF LAND TO FEED FOR A YEAR, OUR COWS IN THE SUMMER ARE ROTATED THROUGH ON AVERAGE 2,000 ACRE PASTURES OF PUBLIC LAND. OUR FEES HELP FUND RESEARCH AND MANAGEMENT OF THE NATURAL HABITAT AND RANGE LAND USE OF NATIVE ELK, MOOSE, BEAR, WOLVES AND MANY OTHER SPECIES CO-EXISTING WITH OUR HERD. THIS SYMBIOTIC RELATIONSHIP BETWEEN COWBOY AND PUBLIC USER HELPS OUR PUBLIC LANDS NOT GO TO THE HIGHEST BIDDER. 

Jessa Brooks rounding up cattle in Ennis, MT.

Cowboy tradition

WE BELIEVE THAT YOUR RELATIONSHIP WITH YOUR FOOD IS AS INTIMATE AS YOUR RELATIONSHIP WITH YOUR HEALTH. COWBOY TRADITION PUTS THE ANIMAL FIRST, THEY ARE YOUR FAMILY AND YOUR LIVELIHOOD. WE BELIEVE THAT LAND RESILIENCE IS OUR RESPONSIBILITY. OVER-GRAZE AND YOUR ANIMALS WILL STARVE NEXT YEAR, DIRTY YOUR WATER SOURCE AND YOUR ANIMALS WILL SICKEN, POORLY MANAGE PREDATORS AND THE FOOD CHAIN WILL WEAKEN.

FAQ

Where can I find Montana beef for sale?

Right here! Montana Brooks Beef is proud to serve Flathead County and our neighboring states. We offer free pickup in Whitefish, MT and Ronan, MT. 

Where is Montana Brooks Beef located for local pickup?

We have two primary hubs for our local customers. You can find our grass-fed beef near Ronan, MT in the beautiful Mission Valley, or coordinate a pickup in Whitefish, MT. This allows us to serve the entire Flathead Valley and Lake County area with the freshest 100% grass-fed beef available.

How do I coordinate a large bulk order pickup?

For half cow or quarter beef orders, we coordinate a specific pickup date at our Ronan or Whitefish locations. Our bulk shares are boxed and fully frozen for easy loading into a truck or SUV.

How do I transport frozen beef back to Idaho or Washington?

Our beef is professionally processed, vacuum-sealed, and labeled to ensure freshness and easy storage. Vacuum-sealed beef can last up to a year in the freezer when properly stored. When placed in a high-quality cooler, it stays safely cool for 12–24 hours of travel time.

How much meat do I get with a quarter cow?

A quarter cow (quarter beef share) from Montana Brooks Beef has been standardized 120 lbs of grass fed beef. Montana Brooks Beef offers a Quarter Beef Box with a variety of cuts, including a curated choice of roasts, steaks, stew-meat, and hamburger.

How much meat do I get with half a cow?

A half a cow (half beef share) from Montana Brooks Beef typically yields approximately 200 lbs of grass fed beef. This is often called the "take-home weight" and depends on the animal's size. Montana Brooks Beef offers a Half Beef Box with a variety of cuts, including a curated choice of roasts, steaks, stew-meat, and hamburger.

How much meat do I get with a full cow?

A full cow (full beef share) from Montana Brooks Beef typically yields approximately 400 lbs of grass fed beef. This is often called the "take-home weight" and depends on the animal's size. Montana Brooks Beef offers a Full Beef Box with your preference of types of steaks, size of your roasts, and the amount of burger you would like in your share. 

Is your beef organic and hormone-free?

While we follow organic principles, we pride ourselves on being 100% grass-fed and grass-finished. Our cattle are never given growth hormones, preventative antibiotics, or mRNA vaccines. Because they graze on diverse Montana pastures, our grass-fed beef is a natural source of CLA and vitamins A and E.

Why is grass-finished beef better than grain-finished?

Grass-finished beef is leaner and contains up to 5 times more Omega-3 fatty acids than grain-finished beef. By choosing Montana grass-finished beef, you are getting a product that is not only better for your heart health but also supports a more natural life for the animal.

Is your beef grass-fed or grain-finished?

Our beef is range and pasture-raised and finished on alfalfa and grass roughage for optimal flavor and tenderness. Increased biodiversity in a cow’s diet improves beef nutrition by delivering a wider range of vitamins, minerals, and beneficial fats—like omega-3s and CLA—resulting in more nutrient-dense, flavorful meat.

Do you use hormones or antibiotics?

We do not use added hormones. Antibiotics are only used when absolutely necessary to ensure animal health, and any treated animals are removed from our beef program.

Do you use regenerative practices?

Yes. A regenerative practice is a journey, Brandon grew up in a ranching family that valued holistic practices and low input farming. We have continued this by reducing our fertilizers, focusing on low or no till and importing nutrients instead of extracting. Our goals are to continue to build top soil to improve drought resistance and nurture our soil biodiversity.

What cuts of beef do you offer?

Our quarter, half and whole beef include the following:

Steaks (Ribeye, T-Bone, New York Strip, Sirloin and Round)

Chuck and Sirloin Tip Roasts

Ground beef

Specialty cuts (Brisket, Short Ribs, Flank, Skirt)

Do you sell bulk beef?

Yes! We offer bulk beef options, including:

Quarter beef

Half beef

Whole beef

Buying in bulk is a great way to stock your freezer and save money per pound.

How is the beef packaged?

Our beef is professionally processed, clear vacuum-sealed, and labeled to ensure freshness and easy storage. Vacuum-sealed beef can last up to a year in the freezer when properly stored.

How do I place an order?

Orders can be placed directly through our website using PayPal or by contacting us. Just place your deposit and we will contact you when your order is ready!

Do you offer shipping?

Currently we are not shipping out of Montana and focusing on feeding our local communities. We do over bulk deliveries for a fee, please reach out if you want to inquire if we deliver to your area. 

How much freezer space do I need for bulk beef?

As a general guide:

Quarter beef: ~6 cubic feet

Half beef: ~12 cubic feet

Whole beef: ~24 cubic feet

How often is beef available?

We start deliveries in December and butcher through the spring. We start taking deposits in August to plan for our winter harvest. 

What if I have an issue with my order?

We guarantee your order and know you will absolutely love it, but in the case something isn’t right we will fix it. Referrals are the foundation of our business, and we take far too much pride in our beef to ever leave an order anything less than right.

Why buy beef directly from a ranch?

Buying direct means:

Higher quality and transparency

Better value for your money

Supporting a local Montana ranch

Knowing exactly where your food comes from
